tech.name: Stateless MCP (Model Context Protocol, spec 2026-07-28)
tech.status: shipped: 2026-07-28 is the current MCP protocol version
tech.one_line: MCP drops the initialize handshake and the session ID: every request carries what it needs, so any server instance can answer it.

predecessor.name: Session-based MCP (spec 2025-11-25): initialize handshake and Mcp-Session-Id

hook.text: You lose your whole order when your waiter goes home. That is how MCP worked until July 28, 2026.

claims.text: In stateful MCP, if the server instance holding a session fails, the session state is lost and the client must reconnect and redo the handshake.
The 2026-07-28 specification was released on July 28, 2026.

before.text: MCP is how AI apps reach their tools. An app first shook hands with one server and could be given a session ID, like a table number. Only that server knew the order; on a busy night the others could not simply step in.

claims.text: MCP is an open protocol connecting LLM applications to external data sources and tools.
The initialize request and initialized notification must be the first interaction between client and server.
A server MAY assign a session ID at initialization in the MCP-Session-Id header; clients MUST include it on all later requests.
A plain load balancer can't route a session's requests to other instances, which lack its state; operators fall back to sticky sessions.

new.text: The MCP specification that shipped on July 28, 2026 removes both: no handshake, no session ID. Every request is a complete order slip that any server can take. State that must be remembered is a ticket (a handle) the server hands back and the app passes in again.

claims.text: The initialize/initialized handshake is removed; every request carries its protocol version and client capabilities in _meta (SEP-2575).
Protocol-level sessions and the Mcp-Session-Id header are removed from Streamable HTTP (SEP-2567).
Servers that need cross-call state mint an explicit handle from a tool, e.g. create_basket() returns basket_id, passed back as an ordinary argument.
SEP-2575 and SEP-2567 have Final status.

why.text: A busy service just adds servers: any request can land on any of them, and if one goes away the next request goes to another.

claims.text: Any request can land on any server instance behind a plain round-robin load balancer without shared storage.
Stateless by default enables horizontal scaling and improves resilience, as any request can be handled by any server instance.

takeaway.text: The fix was never a better waiter; it was moving the memory out of his head and onto the slip. A server that remembers nothing is a server anyone can replace.

claims.text: The protocol no longer manages session state; applications that need state carry it in explicit handles visible to the model.

outro.text: Spoken call to action: subscribe for the next one. On screen: the takeaway card and a Subscribe button. No 'Next' line: the next episode is not decided.

edges.label: 1 handshake, 2 session ID, then every request
